item.title: Tarique, Erdoğan hold bilateral meeting in Antalya
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan held a bilateral meeting in Antalya, Türkiye, on Tuesday to strengthen ties between the two countries.
The meeting began at 7:15pm local time at the Maxx Royal Hotel and lasted around 30 minutes, Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu said.
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman and State Minister-1 for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir were also present at the meeting.
Earlier, the prime minister arrived in Antalya in the afternoon on a three-day visit to attend the World Leaders’ Summit of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31), scheduled for November 11-12, and hold talks with leaders of various countries.
A Turkish Airlines flight carrying the prime minister, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and other members of the entourage landed at Antalya Airport at 4:03pm local time after a stopover in Istanbul.
Tarique departed Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 7:30am Bangladesh time.
The UN climate change conference, COP31, officially began in Antalya on Monday and will continue until November 20.
As part of the conference, the two-day World Leaders’ Summit will be held on November 11-12.
The prime minister is scheduled to address a plenary session on November 12 and hold several bilateral meetings with world leaders on the sidelines of the summit, Foreign Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury said at a briefing in Dhaka on Monday.
In his address, Tarique is expected to outline Bangladesh’s position and priorities on climate justice, the historical responsibility of developed countries, climate finance, adaptation, loss and damage, and climate-resilient sustainable development.
Chowdhury said Bangladesh’s key priorities include securing adaptation finance, addressing loss and damage, and ensuring the effective implementation of developed countries’ climate finance commitments.
Although Bangladesh accounts for only 0.05% of global greenhouse gas emissions, it remains among the countries most vulnerable to climate change, he said, adding that securing climate justice is a key priority for the country.
Bangladesh will also highlight its achievements in climate resilience and share its experience in addressing climate impacts across South Asia and the wider Asian region.
As part of its participation, Bangladesh has taken the initiative to establish a jute pavilion in the conference’s Green Zone to showcase the versatility of jute, its environment-friendly properties and its potential as an alternative to plastic.
A joint declaration between Bangladesh and Türkiye on the use and promotion of jute and jute products is also expected to be signed during the conference, the foreign secretary said.
The Foreign Ministry will organise two side events in the Blue Zone on November 12 and 13. One will focus on gender-based vulnerability in Bangladesh caused by climate change, while the other will address challenges in promoting environment-friendly, biodegradable and zero-waste jute products.
The prime minister is scheduled to leave Antalya for Dhaka at 4:15pm local time on November 12. His flight is expected to arrive in Dhaka at 5:50am on Friday.

item.title: Bomb blasts, arson spread across country, bus driver killed
item.description:
A bus driver was killed in Faridpur as a fresh wave of crude bomb explosions, vehicle arson and violent demonstrations swept through several districts on Tuesday, with police reporting more than 100 explosions near the Padma Bridge toll plaza during an overnight blockade.
At least eight vehicles were burned or set ablaze between early Tuesday and evening, as explosions, clashes and road blockades were reported in Dhaka, Shariatpur, Gopalganj, Chittagong, Manikganj and several other areas.
The violence followed several days of attacks targeting public transport, police facilities, educational institutions and government establishments, prompting authorities to step up security and intelligence operations nationwide.
The latest incidents included a fatal bus fire in Faridpur, explosions and vandalism near the Padma Bridge, a police vehicle torched during clashes in Tungipara, and separate attacks on buses and other vehicles in Savar, Dhamrai, Chittagong, Manikganj and Khagrachhari.
Police Headquarters had earlier reported 22 vehicles torched nationwide over a rolling 24-hour period ending Tuesday morning.
Dhaka continued to experience crude bomb explosions and arson attacks following several days of violence.
Police information published on Tuesday indicated that explosions had been reported at multiple locations across the capital during the preceding day and night.
Among the recent targets were Dhaka University’s Teacher-Student Centre, court premises, educational institutions and busy intersections.
A bus was set on fire beneath the Farmgate metro rail station on Monday evening, while separate explosions were reported in Banasree, Shyampur, Mirpur and other areas.
The incidents followed Sunday’s explosions at several locations on the Dhaka University campus, near the Criminal Investigation Department headquarters in Malibagh and at police facilities.
Police have arrested suspects in connection with some of the attacks and recovered unexploded crude bombs and materials allegedly intended for further incidents.
However, investigators have yet to establish publicly whether all the attacks were coordinated or directed by a single group.
The most serious incident occurred in Faridpur, where 55-year-old bus driver Md Kalachan Sheikh died after unidentified assailants set fire to a parked bus while he was sleeping inside.
Kalachan, a resident of Muksudpur in Gopalganj, was unable to escape as the vehicle caught fire. Police said he died from smoke inhalation.
Faridpur Kotwali Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mahmudul Hasan confirmed the death and said police were investigating the attack.
In one of the most alarming incidents, police reported that more than 100 crude bombs were detonated near the Padma Bridge toll plaza in Shariatpur around 1am Tuesday during a blockade.
The explosions disrupted toll collection and created panic in the surrounding area. Vehicles were also reportedly vandalised during the incident.
Separate arson attacks were reported in Savar and Dhamrai on the outskirts of Dhaka early Tuesday.
A parked bus was set on fire in Dhamrai around 1am, while another bus belonging to Savar Paribahan was torched in the Namagendha area of Savar around 2am.
Firefighters extinguished both fires. No casualties were reported.
In Chittagong, a bus was set ablaze in the Mansurabad area near City Gate, while a truck seized in connection with a case was torched near Chittagong Polytechnic Institute.
A crude bomb also exploded at a Grameen Bank branch in Anwara upazila, triggering a fire that damaged documents. The bank’s security guard brought the blaze under control.
In Khagrachhari, a parked Chander Gari was gutted by fire near KSTC Hospital. A BNP ward office in Guimara was also set ablaze, prompting police to detain six suspects.
A minibus was torched in Manikganj shortly after midnight, following a series of crude bomb explosions reported in the district on Monday evening.
Vehicle arson was also reported in Narayanganj, where two BRTC buses were attacked in Rupganj.
Tensions escalated in Gopalganj on Tuesday as road blockades, demonstrations and clashes disrupted normal activities in several areas.
In Tungipara, a police vehicle was set on fire during clashes involving police and activists allegedly associated with the banned Chhatra League. Shops were vandalised, and injuries were reported.
Demonstrators also blocked roads in parts of the district, while police carried out operations to restore traffic movement and prevent further violence.
The unrest followed crude bomb explosions on Monday night near Gopalganj Government Zilla School, Government Women’s College, the District Shilpakala Academy and the Regional Passport Office, as well as in Kashiani and Kotalipara.
Gopalganj Superintendent of Police Md Habibullah said eight people had been arrested, 15 crude bombs recovered and seven motorcycles seized in connection with the incidents.
Police also reported attempts to obstruct the Dhaka-Khulna highway by placing felled trees and setting fires on the road.
Amid the escalating violence, Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain Fakir held a meeting with senior police officials from across the country on Tuesday.
The meeting, attended by metropolitan police commissioners, range deputy inspectors general and superintendents of police from all 64 districts, reviewed the security situation and measures to prevent further attacks.
The IGP instructed officers to intensify patrols, strengthen intelligence surveillance and identify those involved in arson, crude bomb explosions and other acts of violence.
Additional police were ordered to be deployed in Gopalganj, Shariatpur, Madaripur and Faridpur, where authorities considered the security situation particularly sensitive.
Police sources alleged that individuals linked to the activities-banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations were involved in some of the incidents.
Investigators were also examining allegations that attackers had received financial support or instructions from others.
Those allegations have not been independently established across the full series of attacks.
The violence coincided with a nationwide blockade program announced by the banned Chhatra League, with authorities stepping up security on major highways and around important installations.

item.title: India says Hasina needs travel documents to return
item.description:
India has said travel documents are required for travel as Bangladesh seeks the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina under the existing bilateral treaty.
“Obviously, for travel of people, you need a travel document. That is what I understand. But again, this is a technical matter, and I'll come back to you,” Indian Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told reporters in New Delhi on Tuesday.
Asked whether extradition was possible without a passport, Jaiswal said Hasina’s case was a legal matter that would be dealt with accordingly.
On Monday, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said Bangladesh does not issue passports to “convicted and fled terrorists”. He did not clarify whether the government would issue a one-way travel permit to Hasina, who reportedly wants to return by December.
International Crimes Tribunal Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said on Tuesday that Hasina had no legal recourse left to challenge her verdict, as the 30-day appeal deadline had expired.
“If she genuinely wanted to return to Bangladesh, she would have come back while the trial was ongoing and faced the case,” he told reporters.
Meanwhile, Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman said Hasina had not personally applied for a passport. He said a law firm had sent a letter seeking arrangements for issuing one, but stressed that an application must come from the individual concerned.
The Associated Press reported that London-based law firm Matrix Chambers had emailed the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, seeking a passport and national identity card for Hasina. The letter requested expedited processing, citing her Bangladeshi nationality and international human rights obligations.
A diplomatic source told UNB that the letter, addressed to Acting High Commissioner Preeti Rahman, had been forwarded to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Separately, Jaiswal criticised foreign nationals for allegedly using livestreams and online content to portray Dhaka as Delhi. Asked about reports of Chinese nationals livestreaming from homes and public places, he called such attempts to spread false narratives unfortunate and urged the authorities concerned to take action.

item.title: UN climate chief: Climate crisis reaching pandemic proportions
item.description:
The climate crisis is rapidly becoming a global public health emergency, threatening millions through extreme heat, air pollution, food insecurity and increasingly destructive weather events, UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell warned as COP31 opened in Türkiye.
Describing the crisis as a health emergency of “pandemic proportions”, Stiell said global warming was overwhelming healthcare systems, damaging infrastructure and disproportionately affecting vulnerable communities.
“The world is getting dangerously hot,” he said at a press conference in Antalya on Monday, citing hundreds of millions exposed to extreme heat across southern Asia and an estimated 50,000 heatwave-related deaths in Europe during the northern summer.
His warning came as the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) released its State of the Climate Update 2026, which said the past 12 years had been the warmest on record. Global temperatures from January to September this year averaged around 1.47°C above pre-industrial levels.
WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo warned that a powerful El Niño could push temperatures higher, potentially making 2027 another record-breaking year. Ocean heat content has remained at record levels for the 10th consecutive year, while rising sea levels are increasing risks for an estimated 900 million people living in low-lying coastal areas.
Climate impacts are already being felt through heatwaves, floods, droughts and increasingly intense storms. Nearly 52% of the world's land experienced extreme drought for at least one month in 2025, threatening farmers, outdoor workers and food security.
Stiell also highlighted the growing health risks for pregnant women, newborns and mothers, while Dr Alan Dangour, director of climate and health at the Wellcome Trust, said fossil fuel pollution and human-induced climate change were estimated to cause more than three million deaths annually through air pollution and extreme heat.
Children, older people, pregnant women and outdoor workers remain particularly vulnerable.
Experts said cleaner energy, electrification, heat early-warning systems and stronger healthcare infrastructure could help reduce the risks. Dangour said cleaner air was already preventing more than 300,000 deaths annually in at least 77 countries where fossil fuel-related air pollution had declined over the past decade.
Stiell urged governments to speed up the transition to clean electricity, warning that continued dependence on fossil fuels would impose growing economic and health costs.
“At this COP, nations face a choice: electric or shock,” he said, calling for a shift towards clean energy.
The issue is particularly urgent for developing countries such as Bangladesh, where extreme heat, air pollution and climate-related disasters place additional pressure on communities and healthcare services. Experts stressed the need for climate-resilient health systems, disease surveillance, heat protection and reliable early-warning mechanisms.
Financing is also emerging as a key issue at COP31. Stiell said the Climate and Health Funders Coalition, established at COP30 in Belém, had awarded more than $200 million for climate and health initiatives. The coalition initially committed $300 million and attracted a further $150 million in funding commitments, Dangour said.
Saulo said the number of countries reporting multi-hazard early-warning systems had risen from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025, but stressed that such systems required reliable climate data and sustained investment.
COP31 is expected to build on health-related commitments made at COP30, with Türkiye and Australia prioritising resilient health systems. As negotiations continue, experts are urging governments to put public health at the centre of climate policies rather than treating it as a secondary consequence of global warming.

item.title: Government plans AI education for classes VI-XII from 2027
item.description:
The government plans to introduce artificial intelligence (AI) education in the curriculum for students from Class VI to XII from the 2027 academic year, covering topics such as AI applications, robotics, virtual reality, augmented reality, machine learning and nanotechnology.
The curriculum will also emphasise the responsible use of AI, fact-checking, deepfake detection and online safety.
Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon announced the plan in a statement under Rule 71 during the second day of the fourth session of parliament on Tuesday.
Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal presided over the session.
In his statement, the minister said the world had entered the era of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, making technologies such as nanotechnology, robotics and artificial intelligence increasingly important.
Against this backdrop, the government was placing special emphasis on ICT education and would incorporate AI-related content into the curriculum for Classes VI-XII from the 2027 academic year.
Outlining the class-wise curriculum, Milon said Class VI students would learn about artificial intelligence, AI-powered tools, virtual reality, augmented reality and robotics.
Class VII would cover the use of technology, AI-powered search tools, the use of AI in learning, the Internet of Things (IoT) and its real-life applications.
For Class VIII, the curriculum would include AI assistants, automation, IoT, the use of technology in business and commerce, emerging job opportunities, remote work and freelancing.
Students in Classes IX and X would study the ethical and unethical use of AI, e-commerce, entrepreneurship, the Fourth Industrial Revolution, machine learning, deep learning, robotics and nanotechnology.
At the higher secondary level, students in Classes XI and XII would be introduced to AI, its applications in everyday life and education, and its practical uses across different fields.
The minister said teaching students how to use AI would not be enough; they would also need to learn how to verify and assess information generated by AI tools.
Citing Singapore's inclusion of fact-checking and deepfake-related topics in its school curriculum, he said Bangladeshi students should also be taught responsible, age-appropriate AI use, fact-checking and online safety.
The government also plans to establish technology labs in around 5,000 educational institutions to enhance students' technological skills, the minister said.
The labs will offer training in AI, robotics, 3D printing and renewable energy technologies. The project has an estimated cost of Tk7,500 crore.
Under the Next Generation Secondary Education Project, the government also plans to establish multimedia classrooms, technology labs, science labs and computer labs in 1,050 educational institutions. The project will also cover teacher training and the construction of new classrooms.
Its estimated cost is Tk3,397.49 crore.
Milon said Bangladeshi representatives attended UNESCO's Digital Learning Week, held from September 8 to 11, where the theme was "Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence".
Discussions at the event focused on preventing AI misuse and ensuring its responsible application in education, he added.
Responding to a question from MP Rasheda Begum Hira, the minister said Tk397 crore had been spent on setting up digital labs in 4,000 educational institutions during the first phase of the initiative.
The lawmaker urged the minister to visit his constituency and assess whether the labs were functioning effectively.
In response, Milon said the government had prioritised ICT education and allocated funds for the sector in the national budget.
He said the government was working to meet the expectations raised by the lawmaker and would implement the planned initiatives in the coming days.

item.title: PM seeks deeper, multifaceted defence ties with Turkiye
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has emphasised deepening and diversifying defence cooperation between Bangladesh and Turkiye as he held a bilateral meeting with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Antalya.

Their discussions also covered the ways to strengthen bilateral ties, boost trade and investment, and expand cooperation in energy, minerals, climate action and the Rohingya repatriation.

The prime minister held talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the Max Royal Hotel in Antalya on Tuesday evening, said his Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.

The meeting took place a day before the two-day World Leaders’ Summit of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, scheduled for 11-12 November.

The prime minister stressed making defence cooperation between the two countries deeper and more multifaceted, and called for expanding it alongside joint investment in the defence sector.

He also urged closer dialogue between the two countries to boost bilateral trade and investment.

The prime minister stressed making defence cooperation between the two countries deeper and more multifaceted, and called for expanding it alongside joint investment in the defence sector.

On energy and minerals, the two sides discussed expanding cooperation in energy security and mineral resources. The prime minister said Turkish investors have opportunities in Bangladesh’s renewable energy sector.

The two sides also underscored the importance of forging partnership in the renewable energy sector.

Highlighting climate change, Tarique Rahman stressed the importance of international cooperation for vulnerable countries like Bangladesh in tackling its adverse impacts. He also congratulated Turkiye for hosting COP31.

Turning to the Rohingya crisis, the prime minister appreciated Turkiye’s consistent support.

He expressed gratitude for Ankara’s firm solidarity with the Rohingya at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and for its humanitarian assistance on the ground.

He said Turkiye’s continued support and active role at the United Nations and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) are vital to ensuring the safe, dignified and sustainable repatriation of the Rohingya, and urged Ankara to keep backing them in international forums.

At the beginning of the meeting, Tarique Rahman recalled his meeting with the Turkish president on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York in September. He praised the progress made in bilateral cooperation since then.

Earlier in the day, the prime minister arrived in Antalya on a three-day visit to attend the summit and hold talks with leaders of different countries.

A Turkish Airlines flight carrying him, his wife Zubaida Rahman and other members of the entourage landed at Antalya Airport at 4:03 pm local time after a stopover in Istanbul. He had left Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 7:30 am Bangladesh time.

The prime minister is scheduled to address a plenary session on 12 November and hold several bilateral meetings with world leaders on the sidelines of the summit.

90-day credit facility on 11 commodities imports to curb price hikes ahead of Ramadan
item.description:
Ahead of Ramadan, Bangladesh Bank has allowed the import of 11 essential food commodities under deferred payment facilities to keep market prices affordable and ensure steady supplies.

The central bank issued a circular to this effect today, Wednesday.

According to the directive, importers will be entitled to a deferred payment facility of up to 90 days for importing rice, wheat, onions, pulses, soybean oil, palm oil, sugar, chickpeas, spices, dates and peas.

Bangladesh Bank said this special facility was extended to keep supplies smooth and prices manageable during the Ramadan.

Importers will be able to avail of this credit facility for up to 90 days under suppliers' credit or buyers' credit.

Under this facility, importers will not be required to settle the full import bill immediately upon the arrival of the consignment in the country. Instead, they will have the opportunity to pay the import value at the end of the stipulated period on a deferred basis.

This will allow importers to clear their bank liabilities after selling the goods in the domestic market. Central bank officials believe the move will ease working capital pressures on importers.

Demand for commodities such as rice, pulses, onions, edible oil, sugar, chickpeas and dates typically surges in the country during Ramadan.

Ensuring uninterrupted supplies and reducing price pressure in the retail market become crucial during this period. Banking sector insiders believe this fresh central bank decision will encourage traders to import these essential goods.

Bangladesh Bank stated that this new facility will remain in effect until March 15 next year.

Earlier on 8 November, Bangladesh Bank instructed commercial banks to keep cash margins at a minimum level based on banker-customer relationships when opening letters of credit (LCs) for importing these commodities ahead of Ramadan.

The items were rice, wheat, onions, pulses, soybean oil, palm oil, sugar, chickpeas, peas, spices, and dates.

An LC margin is the specific percentage of cash or security an importer must deposit with a bank when opening an import letter of credit. For example, if a 100 percent margin is imposed, the entire value of the imported goods must be deposited in cash to open an LC.

When the margin requirement is kept at a minimum or relaxed, opening an LC becomes feasible with significantly lower upfront cash deposits based on mutual trust and relations with the bank.

item.title: Why ACC’s press briefing on Asif Mahmud is not illegal: HC
item.description:
The High Court has issued a rule questioning the legality of the Anti-Corruption Commission's (ACC) press briefings concerning Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, former adviser to the interim government and leader of the National Citizen Party (NCP).

The rule was issued on Wednesday by a High Court bench comprising Justice Md Bashir Ullah and Justice Md Hamidur Rahman after an initial hearing on a writ petition filed by Asif Mahmud.

He filed the petition in September, challenging the legality of an ACC press briefing in which the commission announced that it had found “preliminary evidence” after deciding to investigate allegations of corruption and money laundering against him.

The rule asks why the ACC press briefings, held on 2 and 13 September by its deputy director and assistant director, announcing that “preliminary evidence” had been found following the decision to investigate the allegations, should not be declared illegal and beyond lawful authority for violating Article 31 of the Constitution and the ACC's Information Disclosure Policy, 2011.

The court also asked why the ACC should not be directed to refrain from holding press briefings on any ongoing inquiry or investigation.

The hearing on Asif Mahmud's writ petition took place on 4 November. After hearing the petition, the court set this Wednesday for its order.

Senior lawyer Mohammod Hossain, along with lawyers Yousuf Ali and Zahirul Islam Musa, represented the petitioner. Lawyer Mohammad Mahbubur Rahman Khan appeared for the ACC.

Confirming the issuance of the rule, lawyer Zahirul Islam Musa told Prothom Alo that the ACC chairman, deputy director, public relations officer and assistant director had been asked to respond to the rule within four weeks.

According to the petitioner's lawyers, the ACC's deputy director and public relations officer, along with an assistant director, held two press briefings on 2 and 13 September.

At the briefings, the commission said it had found “preliminary evidence” after deciding to investigate allegations of corruption and money laundering against Asif Mahmud.

The briefings violated the protection of dignity and reputation guaranteed under Article 31 of the Constitution and the ACC's Right to Information Disclosure Guidelines, the lawyers argued.

The Awami League government fell on 5 August 2024 following the July Mass Uprising. An interim government led by Professor Muhammad Yunus was formed on 8 August that year.

As a representative of the students who led the July uprising, Asif Mahmud joined the interim government as an adviser. He was initially in charge of the Ministry of Labour and Employment and the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

In November 2024, he was given charge of the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives. He subsequently served as adviser to both the local government and youth and sports ministries.

Asif Mahmud resigned from the interim government in December 2025. Later that month, he formally joined the National Citizen Party (NCP). He is currently the party's senior joint member secretary.

BANGLADESH-GARMENTS/

Before dawn each day, garment worker Shilpi Khatun cooks over a wood-fired clay stove because her family cannot afford gas, before heading to a factory in Gazipur, an industrial hub on the outskirts of Dhaka.

The 27-year-old is the sole breadwinner in a household where her husband is unemployed and her parents and in-laws depend on her wages.

Rising prices have left Khatun struggling to afford basic necessities despite five years in the garment industry, a frustration shared by thousands of Bangladesh's garment workers who staged protests last week demanding the minimum monthly wage be raised to Tk 30,000 ($242.82) from Tk 12,500.

"Everything costs more now. Rent has doubled, food is more expensive and whatever I earn disappears before the month is over," Khatun said as she gathered leafy greens outside her home to eat with rice for lunch.

Wage pressure mounts

Last week's unrest, some of it violent, forced hundreds of factories to shut down as workers staged protests and clashed with police, who used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse demonstrators.

The government's wage board agreed on 4 November to implement a revised wage structure from December, with workers set to receive their first pay under the new scale in January, but has yet to determine the size of the increase.

Parveen and her two daughters often live on little more than rice and vegetables, with meat and fish becoming luxuries beyond their reach. To cut costs, one of her daughters dropped out of school.

Low labour costs have helped make Bangladesh the world's second-largest apparel exporter after China and a preferred manufacturing base for global brands including H&M, Zara, Gap, Primark and Walmart. The industry generates more than 80 per cent of the country's export earnings and employs more than 4 million people.

Manufacturers, however, say a steep wage increase would erode Bangladesh's cost advantage over rivals such as India and Vietnam and further squeeze margins already under pressure from higher energy costs.

Workers also receive a 9 per cent annual increment and two festival bonuses in addition to their basic wages, manufacturers say, arguing there is limited room for substantial pay increases.

Workers make stark choices

Workers like Khatun say the wage increase has not kept pace with rising prices, forcing them to make difficult choices over everyday spending.

On the hardest days, Khatun's family survives on puffed rice, she said. Sitting in the small tin-shed room she shares with her husband, she said she had not seen a doctor in three years despite worsening health problems.

Her salary has crept up over five years but not enough to match rising costs. She now earns Tk 13,500 ($108), up from Tk 9,000 when she started. With overtime, she earns about Tk 16,000 but the money rarely lasts until the next payday, she said.

Bangladesh has faced a prolonged cost-of-living squeeze since 2022, with inflation averaging around 9 per cent. Food prices initially drove the surge, but non-food costs have remained high.

"I think twice before buying anything, even food," said Roksana Parveen, a 29-year old sewing operator in a factory in Ashulia on the outskirts of Dhaka. "I know my daughters should be eating better, but I just can't afford it."

item.title: Biman flights on Dhaka–Riyadh–Dhaka route suspended for 19 days
item.description:
Considering the attack-related situation in Saudi Arabia and the safety of passengers, Biman Bangladesh Airlines has decided to extend the suspension of flights on the Riyadh route for another 19 days.

Regular flights on the Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka route will be suspended until 30 November.

This information was provided by Biman Bangladesh Airlines in a press release this Wednesday afternoon.

The statement mentioned that in light of the recent airstrike-related situation in Saudi Arabia and concerns over passenger safety, the previously made decisions regarding the operation of flights to Saudi Arabia will remain in effect until 30 November.

However, flights on the Dhaka-Jeddah, Dhaka-Dammam, and Dhaka-Madinah routes will continue as per the earlier announcements and schedules.

Passengers are requested to contact the nearest Biman sales centre for updated information on tickets and travel.

Earlier, on 25 October, the suspension period of flights on the Dhaka-Dammam and Dhaka-Riyadh routes was extended until 4 November.

Later, the company announced the resumption of regular flights on the Dhaka-Dammam-Dhaka route starting 7 November.

However, it was decided to keep the Riyadh route's flights suspended until further notice.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) reported on 8 November that 186 flights operating directly or via transit between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia were disrupted due to restrictions on flight operations following attacks by Iran-supported Yemeni armed group Houthis at various Saudi Arabian airports. Among these, there were 109 direct flights.

item.title: COP31 pledge targets $156b annual investment to boost electrification
item.description:
Governments, energy agencies and businesses have pledged to accelerate global electrification, with an annual investment commitment of $156 billion for power grids, renewable energy and storage announced at the COP31 climate summit on Tuesday.
The COP31 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge aims to raise electricity’s share of global final energy consumption from around 23% to at least 35% by 2035, accelerating the shift to electric transport, buildings and industries. It has received backing from 180 companies with combined annual revenues of $1.69 trillion.
COP31 President Murat Kurum said electrification was essential to strengthen energy security, reduce emissions and support economic growth, particularly amid growing concerns over dependence on imported energy.
The Utilities for Net Zero Alliance (UNEZA) raised its annual investment commitment from $148 billion to $156 billion. The International Energy Agency (IEA) will track progress through a global monitoring mechanism, while the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) will help developing countries identify investment needs and access financing.
The COP31 presidency is also establishing an Electrify Now Finance Coalition, bringing together governments, development banks and private financial institutions to mobilise funding for emerging and developing economies. The World Bank and African Development Bank are set to serve as its inaugural co-chairs in 2027.
However, campaigners have questioned whether rising electricity demand will be met with renewable energy or additional fossil fuel generation.
Claire Smith of the civil society coalition Beyond Fossil Fuels warned that electrification could increase fossil fuel consumption unless accompanied by renewable energy expansion, stronger grids and storage facilities. The pledge does not explicitly require all additional electricity to come from clean sources, leaving countries to determine their own energy mix.
Türkiye's continued investment in oil and gas has also raised questions about the consistency of its climate ambitions. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan recently announced two new oil fields with an estimated combined potential of 135 million barrels, while reporting daily production of 84,000 barrels in the Gabar region.
Climate Action Tracker rates Türkiye's overall climate action as “critically insufficient”, citing continued investment in fossil fuels despite progress in wind and solar energy.
The debate has particular significance for developing countries such as Bangladesh, where dependence on imported fossil fuels, limited access to affordable finance and inadequate infrastructure remain major challenges. Expanding renewable energy, upgrading distribution networks and securing technology and investment will be crucial to a sustainable transition.
Further discussions on climate finance are scheduled for November 13. The broader challenge for COP31 will be to turn investment pledges into measurable action and ensure that electrification delivers affordable, reliable and cleaner energy without deepening debt or prolonging fossil fuel dependence.
**This story was produced as part of the COP31 Climate Change Media Partnership, a journalism fellowship organised by Internews' Earth Journalism Network, Informed Earth and the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.

item.title: Dengue: 4 more die, 1,900 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Four dengue patients died in the last 24 hours till 8am on Wednesday, while 1,900 were hospitalized after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatalities have raised the country's dengue death toll to 478 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalized dengue patients, 780 were in Dhaka Division, 85 in Mymensingh Division, 242 in Chittagong Division, 226 in Khulna Division, 198 in Rajshahi Division, 109 in Rangpur Division, 249 in Barisal Division and 11 in Sylhet Division.
According to the report, a total of 155,668 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalized across the country this year.
So far, 149,123 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito-borne disease last year.

item.title: Home minister: 316 killed in armed group attacks in CHT over five years
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said that 316 people were killed in attacks by armed groups in the Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) over the past 5 years, including 308 civilians and 8 members of the security forces.
During the same period, 435 civilians and 55 members of the security forces were injured.
The home minister provided the information on behalf of the prime minister in response to a written question from SA Jinnah Kabir, member of parliament for Manikganj-1, during the question-and-answer session on the third day of the fourth session of the National Parliament on Wednesday.
In his question, SA Jinnah Kabir sought information on attacks, abductions, forcible extortion and the use of illegal firearms by armed groups, as well as attacks on members of the army and other law enforcement agencies.
He also asked about incidents affecting the security of Bengalis and people from different small ethnic groups living in the CHT districts of Rangamati, Khagrachhari and Bandarban over the past 5 years, including the number of people killed and injured.
In response, Salahuddin Ahmed said armed groups had carried out 97 attacks on security forces over the past 5 years. During this period, 194 attacks targeted the Bengali community and 81 targeted small ethnic groups.
In addition, 297 people were abducted, forcible extortion was carried out in 471 incidents, and illegal firearms were used in 377 incidents.
Outlining the government's measures to control the security situation in the hill districts, the home minister said the special armed forces operation, "Operation Uttaran", was ongoing to maintain peace and order and suppress terrorist activities.
He said the Bangladesh Army, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), police and SRB had increased regular patrols and intelligence activities to prevent terrorist activities.
A strict policy had also been adopted against illegal arms holders, extortionists and terrorists in the hills, he said. Cases were being filed under existing laws over specific allegations of crimes, and the accused were being brought under the law.
The home minister further said regular special joint operations were being conducted by the army, BGB, police and SRB to eliminate the activities of new and old regional armed groups in the CHT and recover illegal firearms.
Based on intelligence information, operations were also being conducted to destroy secret hideouts and training camps of terrorists in remote hilly areas. Helicopters were being used with assistance from the air force when required.
He said the sources and economic sectors linked to terrorists' forcible extortion were being identified and monitored.
To prevent extortion, the number of checkpoints had been increased, while intelligence surveillance of financial transactions, including mobile banking, had been strengthened.
Mentioning that the BGB's capabilities had been increased to prevent the smuggling of illegal firearms and drugs across the border, the minister said surveillance had been intensified in remote areas adjacent to the Mizoram border in India and the Myanmar border.
Police and SRB were also uncovering various sources and networks in the plains involved in supplying weapons and military uniforms, he added.
The home minister further said hundreds of active members of various regional armed groups had been arrested through continuous and special joint operations in the hills.
During these operations, advanced firearms, live ammunition, magazines, combat uniforms, drones and signal equipment used by the groups had been recovered.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,295 as six die in 24 hours
item.description:
Six more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,295.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all six of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,190, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the six new suspected fatalities, the highest concentrations were recorded in the Dhaka and Mymensingh divisions, with two deaths each.
A total of 1,351 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 242,907.
During the same period, 113 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 24,723.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 216,806 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 207,903 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: The world’s largest jade mines are fueling Myanmar’s civil war
item.description:
The mountains of Hpakant in northern Myanmar have been gouged into a honeycomb of scars.
Men carrying pickaxes swarm over heaps of earth dumped by mining companies, hunting for rocks that could be worth a fortune.
Hpakant holds the world’s most valuable jade.
For about a decade, Aung Kyaw drove dump trucks at the mines.
The wages were better than anything he could earn at his farm in central Myanmar.
“I needed to pay for my children’s schooling and health care for my mother,” Aung Kyaw, who asked to use a pseudonym because of fears for his safety, said.
But when the military seized power in Myanmar in a coup five years ago, the relative calm in the area came to a halt.
Locals, artisanal miners and community groups turned their focus from the mines to protesting the ousting of a democratic government, while the ethnic guerilla force, the Kachin Independence Army (KIA), fought the military.
“When heavy clashes broke out, Hpakant became completely unstable,” Aung Kyaw said.
As the military cracked down on mass protests, mining operations gradually resumed.
Aung Kyaw returned to Hpakant but he was out of work.
Many small-scale Kachin miners could no longer get permits or were pushed off their land as the military and KIA seized control of more mining land.
But he came across a Chinese businessman looking for a driver who knew the local terrain well enough to take jade north by truck to the border.
Aung Kyaw applied.
The pay was about 700,000 kyat ($477) a trip, more than double his previous mining wage.
He said despite the risk of being killed: “It was a solid income, that’s why I agreed.”
Jade is mostly sold to buyers from China, where it is thought to symbolize purity of spirit and bring good luck.
There are two types of jade: nephrite, which is sourced from numerous countries, and the fine-quality jadeite that comes primarily from Myanmar and can reach prices higher than some diamonds due to the rarity of its finest grades.
Since the coup, more Chinese buyers have been travelling directly to the mines to identify raw stones to be smuggled out, miner Sai Myo Htwe said.
“Once they have collected a large amount, they hand them over to ‘carriers’,” he said, referring to smugglers.
Previously, some jade passed through established markets in Mandalay and the official emporiums in the country’s capital, Naypyidaw, where stones could be taxed and auctioned.
Now, most stones are smuggled directly over the border to China via two main back roads.
Aung Kyaw and other Kachin locals described routes that avoided towns, winding through jungle with steep climbs, mud and boulders, and driving alongside active combat zones.
They said armed men ran checkpoints every 10 to 15 kilometers, some belonging to the KIA and others aligned with the military.
“Whoever is holding the gun, we just pay the fees as instructed by the bosses,”
Aung Kyaw said.
He said the operation was usually split into three legs, coordinated between several drivers and vehicles, with the last leg crossing the N’Mai River.
“While paying your way through checkpoints, if there are active clashes in certain areas, you have to stop wherever you are, and sometimes you even have to sleep overnight in the jungle and wait it out before moving on,” Aung Kyaw said.
Drivers are sometimes ordered to deliver bribes, including premium liquor or parcels, without knowing what is inside, he said.
Last year Aung Kyaw was detained for three days.
He later learned that a regional commander was in dispute with his team’s leadership.
Another driver came under fire in the jungle, surrendered under a white flag and was released only after explaining he worked for a Chinese carrier group, Aung Kyaw said.
His bullet-riddled vehicle had to be replaced.
“Even worse are the unpredictable threats, such as the danger of landmines, getting hit by heavy artillery shells, or facing air strikes,” Aung Kyaw said.
Hpakant is a vast open-pit mining region, with satellite data showing new pits continually opening.
“The miners are literally moving mountains. The quantity of earth is quite staggering,” said International Crisis Group analyst Thomas Kean.
In the first years after the coup, the military held direct control.
But two years ago, the KIA launched a major offensive, capturing large stretches of land along the Chinese border.
Fighting around Hpakant also intensified.
The mines are now divided between the KIA’s political arm, called the Kachin Independence Organization (KIO), and the military, with a contested zone in the surrounding areas.
A 2015 report from international investigative NGO Global Witness estimated Myanmar’s jade production was worth as much as $US31 billion ($45 billion) a year, with 90 per cent of Hpakant-mined jade smuggled into China.
Under Aung San Suu Kyi’s government, officials tried to reform the industry to curb environmental destruction, improve safety, limit the influence of the military and recover tax lost to smuggling.
In contrast, since the coup, jade sales at official auctions have continued, but remain opaque and no central body publishes production records.
“Myanmar’s jade industry is somewhat of an unregulated free-for-all,” the Global Witness report said.
“The industry is worth billions of dollars, but because it’s all smuggled, we don’t have a clear picture of what it is worth,” Mr Kean explained.
“Controlling Hpakant is very lucrative. The biggest change since the 2021 coup has been the direct contest for territorial control, because controlling territory now means controlling the [unofficial] taxation.”
Despite the KIA and military fighting for decades, they also cooperate to share jade profits, entrenching a system of corruption that enriches armed elites while denying local communities the benefits, according to the International Crisis Group.
The ABC tried to contact the Myanmar military and KIA’s top commander but did not receive a response.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has periodically launched anti-corruption campaigns that have temporarily curbed large-scale illicit cash flows used by Chinese businesses to buy unrecorded Myanmar jade.
“The corruption crackdown in China really took the wind out of the market because jade was this store of value if you had a huge amount of cash and you wanted to convert it into something that was portable,” Mr Kean said.
China’s Foreign Ministry has said it is unaware of any allegations of Chinese companies’ involvement in jade smuggling.
The wealth beneath Kachin’s mountains has rarely translated into prosperity for locals.
Hand-pickers can spend days searching for jade and find nothing, leaving them with not enough money for food.
Many migrant workers sleep in cramped tents near unstable slopes, where landslides pose a constant risk.
Small mining plots run by Kachin families were once common.
ND Seng grew up in Hpakant and her brother still works in the mines.
“As a family we would go and look for rocks, and if we found one, we all shared the earnings,” she said, using a pseudonym because of her fears for her brother’s safety.
Since the coup, she said, some Kachin families have been pushed off their plots as conflict between the military and KIA continues, while many migrant workers have decided the safety risks are too great.
Kachin activist May Sabe Phyu said jade had brought more misery than wealth.
“The conflict is more severe. People are displaced again and again.”
Seng Htoi from the Kachin Women’s Association Thailand (Kwat) said the conflict had deepened a wider cycle of lawlessness, including a thriving drug trade.
Aung Kyaw said drugs had become so prevalent that he sometimes relocated from a boarding house to a local monastery, which was itself overcrowded with families fleeing air strikes.
Activists have called for a global ban on Myanmar gemstones.
“There is no way to buy jade from Myanmar and be sure it is ethically traded,” said Min Tent, of Burma Campaign UK.
Justice for Myanmar has urged Australia and other countries to ban gem imports from Myanmar.
“Australia has still not taken any action to target the junta’s revenue from natural resources,” spokesperson Yadanar Maung said.
Unlike some countries, Australia has not imposed sanctions on the state-owned Myanmar Gems Enterprise (MGE) and it is legal to trade jade sourced from Myanmar.
The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade did not comment on MGE but said it condemned the regime’s “brutal and ongoing atrocities” against the people of Myanmar.
DFAT said Australia had sanctioned 21 individuals in Myanmar in response to systematic human rights abuses and the overthrow of democratically elected leaders, as well as five entities involved in funding the regime’s access to weapons and jet fuel.
In the main jade market, China, there is no move to impose a boycott.
“Within China, there’s not the same kind of activists and lobby groups, you don’t have a ‘Free Myanmar campaign’,” Mr Kean said, citing China’s restricted political environment.
“It’s very hard to persuade people, you know, not to buy these products when there is that cultural attachment.”
In Australia, gem dealer Wai Yan said he avoided buying jade from Hpakant and from government-run auctions where sales went to the military junta.
He said he also avoided buying from China for the same reason.
Mr Wai said his company, Mays Gems, instead bought gems from Yangon or Mandalay and “from smaller miners, the families that work around the big corporations.”
“It’s very difficult to source jade, especially from Burma, because of the political situation,” he said.
And he said many customers were more concerned about whether their jade was genuine than about where it came from.
He believed it was possible to ethically buy jade from smaller miners and that his proceeds were not going towards the military.
Fiona Frith, international jewellery director at auction house Bonhams, said most jade pieces it handled came from China, and had been passed down through families with little information about where the stone was originally mined.
“We can’t physically say where something is from by looking at it,” she told the ABC.
She said Bonhams generally steered clear of jade that had a certificate stating Myanmar as the origin, particularly since the coup, putting it in the same category as ivory.
Australian-based Gem Rock Auctions is a marketplace for third-party sellers from around the world. It has several listings of gemstones from Myanmar.
CEO Ross Sedawie said most of the jade traded on the platform was from artisanal miners or had been in the market for a long time and they had travelled to Thailand to meet sellers and verify they were who they claimed to be.
He said believed it was possible to ethically buy jade from Myanmar from artisanal sellers, but that it was getting harder.
His business required verified sellers in Thailand and China to agree to conditions that a sale didn’t benefit a military-linked company or other armed group.
However, ultimately, he acknowledged there was no way to be certain.
“That supply chain is just so hard to police. We just have to take it on face value,” he told the ABC.

item.title: Iran says tanker struck mine, caught fire in Hormuz
item.description:
Iran’s army said Wednesday that an oil tanker had struck a mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, where the country has been targeting ships that transit without its authorization.
Since the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorized by the Islamic Republic.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.
The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait.
“Early this morning, a violating oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in an unsafe, prohibited area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz,” the naval forces of Iran’s army said in a statement carried by state TV.
In recent weeks Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships had caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.
US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, has been escorting ships through the waterway and said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
On Tuesday, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said three oil tankers had caught fire in Hormuz.
India’s shipping minister later said a Liberia-flagged tanker carrying Indian seafarers had been hit by a projectile in the Gulf.
“Four crew members were injured in the attack, including one Indian national, who suffered minor injuries and was safely taken ashore for further medical examination,” Sarbananda Sonowal said in a post on X.
The remaining 18 crew members, including five Indians, were safe, he added.
It was not clear if the tanker was among those the Revolutionary Guards said had been hit.

item.title: Sakhawat: Bangladesh targets universal health coverage by 2030
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to achieving universal health coverage (UHC) by 2030, saying the government is working to ensure essential healthcare for everyone, regardless of location or social status.
He made the remarks at the first BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Conference in Colombo, Sri Lanka, attended by health ministers, policymakers and experts from member countries.
Sakhawat highlighted progress in reducing maternal and neonatal mortality, maintaining the country’s polio-free status and expanding immunisation programs.
He said HPV vaccination coverage had risen from 2% to more than 85% since the formation of the new government, with a target of reaching full coverage by the end of November.
The minister said the government, under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s leadership, had doubled the health sector budget to 1.01% of GDP, with plans to gradually raise it to 5%.
He outlined plans to strengthen preventive and primary healthcare, including establishing primary healthcare centres in more than 4,600 unions and upgrading upazila health complexes from 50 to 151 beds.
Other initiatives include introducing solar power at major government health facilities, improving medical waste management at 15 major hospitals and adopting the One Health approach.
The government is also working to introduce an integrated electronic health record system and unique e-Health IDs to digitise healthcare services.
To strengthen regional health security, Sakhawat proposed setting up a BIMSTEC Regional Genetic Disease Observatory and Early Warning System.
He stressed the importance of regional cooperation in tackling non-communicable diseases, climate-related health risks, antimicrobial resistance and pandemics, saying Bangladesh was ready to work with other member states through joint initiatives and knowledge-sharing.

item.title: Nearly 4m children contract pneumonia in Bangladesh annually
item.description:
Nearly four million children contract pneumonia in Bangladesh every year, with around 677,000 requiring hospitalisation and an estimated 24,000 dying from the disease, according to research by icddr,b.
The figures were presented at a joint press conference by the Bangladesh Lung Foundation and the Chest and Heart Association of Bangladesh in May 2026.
The country observes World Pneumonia Day today under the theme “A New Era in Pneumonia Control”.
Pneumonia accounts for around 24% of deaths among children under five in Bangladesh, compared with the global average of about 14%, according to the research. The country’s pneumonia mortality rate stands at 7.4 deaths per 1,000 live births, against the Sustainable Development Goal target of three per 1,000 by 2025.
The global toll remains high. UNICEF estimates that more than 700,000 children under five die from pneumonia every year, averaging around 2,000 deaths a day. South Asia has one of the highest infection rates, with more than 2,500 cases per 100,000 children annually.
According to the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation’s 2023 Global Burden of Disease estimates, pneumonia caused around 2.5 million deaths worldwide that year, including approximately 610,000 children under five.
Although respiratory infections often increase in winter, doctors say children can develop pneumonia at any time of the year. Malnutrition, low birth weight, age below six months and exposure to air pollution increase the risk.
Vehicle emissions, construction dust, industrial pollution and smoke from household cooking can damage children’s respiratory systems and make them more vulnerable to pneumonia and other infections.
Data from Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute show that 3,103 children with pneumonia were admitted in 2022. The number rose to 3,511 in 2023 and 4,118 by December 12, 2024. The hospital recorded 2,136 cases up to November 12, 2025.
Separately, the Directorate General of Health Services reported that 175,175 pneumonia patients had been admitted to public hospitals by September 24, 2026. However, the figures cover different reporting periods and populations and cannot be used to establish a direct year-on-year national trend.
Professor Dr Probir Kumar Sarker of the paediatric pulmonology department at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute said delayed treatment could quickly worsen a child's condition.
He said vaccination and improved treatment had helped reduce child deaths from pneumonia, but many children still arrive at hospitals with severe complications. Delays in seeking care and declining antibiotic effectiveness can make treatment more difficult.
The institute treats around 8,000 children a year for pneumonia and other respiratory conditions, including approximately 5,000 pneumonia and 3,000 bronchitis cases, he said.
Doctors advise parents to seek medical attention if a child with fever, cough or cold develops rapid or difficult breathing, or if the lower chest sinks inward while breathing. Severe cases may require oxygen and hospital care.
Doctors stress that routine immunisation, adequate nutrition and a clean environment are essential to preventing pneumonia. The pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) helps protect children against pneumonia caused by pneumococcal bacteria.
Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months, followed by age-appropriate complementary foods, also helps strengthen a child's immunity. Children should be kept away from smoke and air pollution.
The World Health Organization and UNICEF recommend treatment based on the type and severity of the illness. Antibiotics are not needed for every cough or respiratory infection and should be used only following a doctor's assessment.

item.title: Nusrat Tabassum’s Kushtia home gutted in fire, petrol bomb attack alleged
item.description:
A fire destroyed five rooms at the ancestral home of National Citizen Party (NCP) lawmaker Nusrat Tabassum in Kushtia’s Daulatpur upazila early Thursday, with party leaders alleging that assailants hurled petrol bombs at the property.
The blaze broke out shortly after midnight at the lawmaker’s village home in Bagowan.
Firefighters brought it under control around 1:50am, but five of the eight rooms in the single-storey, tin-roofed house were destroyed. Two goats also died in the fire.
NCP leaders alleged that the house was deliberately targeted in a petrol bomb attack and blamed individuals linked to the Awami League.
Police, however, said they had yet to establish the cause of the fire or confirm whether any incendiary devices had been used.
Additional Superintendent of Police Delwar Hossain of the Bheramara Circle said that firefighters rushed to the scene after receiving information about the blaze.
He said the fire caused extensive damage to the house but did not spread to a nearby three-storey building where Tabassum’s parents were staying.
According to the police official, no family members sustained burn injuries.
In a Facebook post, the NCP’s media cell alleged that individuals it described as “Awami terrorists” had thrown petrol bombs at the lawmaker’s residence.
NCP spokesperson Asif Mahmud Sajib Bhuiyan also alleged in a separate Facebook post that the property had been targeted in a petrol bomb attack.
Tabassum is a joint convener of the NCP and a member of its Political Council, the party’s highest policymaking body.
She represents a reserved women’s seat in the 13th National Parliament.
Additional Superintendent of Police Delwar Hossain said investigators had not established whether the fire resulted from a petrol bomb attack.
Fire service personnel remained at the scene to examine the damage and determine the origin of the blaze.
Police said the exact cause would be established following an investigation.

item.title: Jute export earnings rise by 25% in Jul-Oct’FY27
item.description:
Earnings from the jute and jute product exports have risen by 24.88 percent in the first four months from (July-October) of FY27 compared to the corresponding period of FY26.
The export earnings reached $346.37 million during July-October of FY27, up from $277.37 million in the corresponding period of FY26, according to the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB).
The development came amid growing global demand for environment-friendly and natural fibre-based products.
Among the major export items, raw jute recorded the highest growth. Earnings from raw jute exports rose to $53.94 million during the first four months of the current fiscal year from $33.21 million in the same period last year, registering a growth of 62.42%.
Jute yarn and twine, which account for the largest share of the sector's export earnings, also recorded significant growth.
Exports of these products generated $216.54 million during July-October of FY27, compared to $165.70 million in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, marking a 30.68% increase.
However, exports of sacks and bags declined to $53.43 million from $57.72 million during the period. Earnings from other jute products increased to $22.46 million from $20.74 million.
The growing international demand for jute products as alternatives to plastic has opened up new opportunities for Bangladesh. Jute bags, packaging materials, home furnishing products, technical textiles and fashion items are gaining popularity in international markets.
Jute-based charcoal, produced from jute sticks, and other diversified products also hold considerable export potential. Expanding production and exports of these products could help Bangladesh earn additional foreign exchange beyond traditional jute goods.
To tap this potential, the government has taken an initiative to formulate a five-year Bangladesh Jute Sector Development Strategy and Action Plan for 2026-2031.
One of its major targets is to increase annual export earnings from jute and jute goods to $1.64 billion by 2031.
The strategy also aims to raise annual raw jute production from 11.5 million bales to 12 million bales and meet 85%-90% of the country's demand for jute seeds through domestic production.
Product diversification and value addition have received special attention in the proposed strategy.
Currently, value-added products account for around 45% of Bangladesh's total jute product exports. The government aims to increase this share to 70% by 2031.
To achieve the target, the strategy envisages expanding the production of geotextiles, eco-friendly packaging materials, home furnishing products, technical textiles and jute-based industrial goods.
It also emphasizes research, modern technology, product quality improvement and expansion into international markets. The proposed strategy envisages an investment of around Tk 4,750 crore for its implementation.
Prime Minister's Adviser on the ministries of Finance and Planning Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir told BSS that the government has taken initiatives to provide necessary policy support for the development of promising export sectors, including jute and jute goods, alongside the readymade garment industry.
"To achieve this objective, the government is focusing on strengthening the capacities of promising industrial sectors, attracting new investment and diversifying the country's export basket," he added.
President of the Bangladesh Jute Diversified Products Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BJDPMEA) Md Rashedul Karim Munna told BSS that the increase in jute exports, particularly raw jute, is encouraging for the sector.
However, Bangladesh still lags behind in exporting value-added jute products, he said.
He said the country's annual export earnings from jute and jute goods could reach $2 billion to $3 billion if Bangladesh strengthens its capacity to diversify jute applications and manufacture high-value products.
Munna stressed the need for research, product development and appropriate policy support to achieve this target.
He said the government should formulate a well-planned strategic action plan and establish a specialized service centre for research and product development.
"Such a centre would provide entrepreneurs with technical assistance in product design, quality improvement and production technology in line with international market requirements," he added.

item.title: Govt to revise budget for FY27
item.description:
The government has imposed restrictions on new government building construction, vehicle purchases and foreign training funded by public money as part of its measures while preparing the revised budget for FY27.
The Finance Division issued a budget circular on November 9, directing ministries and divisions to reduce expenditure, limit development projects, and prioritize essential sectors.
According to the circular, the revised budget expenditure must not exceed the total ceiling set in the original budget for FY27. Funds from the development budget cannot be transferred to the operating budget.
The government has suspended new residential, non-residential and other government building construction, except facilities under the Ministries of Education, Health and Agriculture. However, projects with at least 70 percent physical progress may receive funds with Finance Division approval. Other urgent construction projects will also require separate approval.
Allocations for purchasing all types of vehicles have also been suspended. Exceptions include replacing TO&E-listed vehicles more than 10 years old and purchasing essential vehicles for newly established government institutions, subject to Finance Division approval.
Except for ambulances and security vehicles, all newly purchased or replacement cars and jeeps must be fully electric. The condition may be relaxed for development projects approved before July 8, 2026.
The circular also bars allocations for land acquisition under the operating budget and interest-free car purchase advances for government employees.
Government-funded foreign training, seminars, symposiums and workshops have been suspended. Limited allocations may be retained for essential foreign visits and training with approval from the competent authorities. Ministries have also been asked to ensure austerity in spending on hospitality, seminars and official events.
For preparing revised revenue and operating expenditure estimates, ministries must consider actual revenue and expenditure trends during the first six months of the previous two fiscal years and the first four months of the current fiscal year. Salary and allowance estimates should follow the National Pay Scale 2026.
Regarding the revised Annual Development Program (ADP), the circular directs ministries to limit the number of projects and prioritize the government's strategic objectives, electoral manifesto and essential development needs.
Priority will go to projects involving foreign loans and grants, human development, agriculture, power generation, agro-based industries, poverty reduction, climate change, disaster management and rehabilitation. Projects scheduled for completion in FY27 will also receive priority.
The circular recommends merging small projects with similar objectives into cluster projects and excluding projects without allocations from the main revised ADP.
It also directs ministries to reduce allocations for slow-moving projects and redirect funds to priority projects with faster implementation prospects, while ensuring adequate local currency allocations for completing ongoing projects on time.
All revised budget proposals must receive scrutiny and approval from the respective Budget Management Committees, with meeting minutes submitted alongside the proposals. Ministries must also update their revenue collection, expenditure and annual procurement plans after approval.
The Finance Division has set November 26 as the deadline for submitting revised operating budget and non-ADP scheme estimates. Revised ADP and project estimates must also reach the Finance Division and relevant divisions of the Planning Commission by the same date.

item.title: BB allows 90-day credit facility for importing 10 essential commodities
item.description:
The Bangladesh Bank has allowed importers to make deferred payments for up to 90 days for imports of 10 essential commodities ahead of the holy month of Ramadan to ensure adequate supplies and keep prices stable in the market.
The Foreign Exchange Policy Department-1 of Bangladesh Bank issued a circular in this regard Wednesday.
Under the new directive, the facility will cover imports of rice, wheat (flour), onion, lentils, edible oil, sugar, chickpeas, peas, spices and dates.
Importers can bring in these commodities under suppliers’ credit or buyers’ credit arrangements and pay for the imports within a maximum of 90 days after receiving the goods.
Bangladesh Bank spokesperson and Executive Director Arief Hossain Khan said the initiative aims to keep the prices of commodities that experience higher demand during Ramadan within the purchasing capacity of ordinary consumers.
He said the central bank had given banks the opportunity to facilitate imports under buyers’ or suppliers’ credit for up to 90 days so that importers could take advance steps to bring in adequate supplies.
“Importers will be able to pay for the imported goods after 90 days,” he said.
Khan said Bangladesh Bank did not want consumers to face additional pressure from rising commodity prices during Ramadan. The circular aims to ensure that people can purchase essential goods at relatively affordable prices, he added.
He also said any mismatch between supply and demand could push up commodity prices. Allowing imports ahead of Ramadan would help importers bring in sufficient quantities of goods, prevent shortages and ease upward pressure on prices.
According to the Bangladesh Bank circular, the facility has been introduced for commercial imports to maintain the normal supply of essential food commodities during Ramadan and keep prices at tolerable levels.
Importers will not have to pay the full import value immediately and can settle the payment within 90 days.
The circular said an earlier directive, FEPD-1 Circular No. 30, issued on August 13, had allowed deferred-payment imports of certain commodities under Part-D, paragraph 1(1).
The latest decision expands the facility to cover additional important food commodities ahead of Ramadan.
Other instructions under the previous circular will remain unchanged. Bangladesh Bank has also instructed authorized dealer banks to inform their respective clients about the new directive.

Tehran has designated Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organisations," Iran's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday, in a reciprocal move following Buenos Aires' designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards as a terrorist entity in April.

Argentina had designated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organisation, following a push from US President Donald Trump's administration for allies to do so.

Iran's Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday that Tehran considers the Argentinian air force and navy terrorist organisations "based on the principle of reciprocity".

"It is evident that the responsibility for all consequences arising from this matter will lie with the Argentine government," the ministry added, without elaborating. It made no mention of Argentina's army.

In a statement on Wednesday, Argentina's foreign ministry said it "categorically rejects" Iran's decision.

Argentina said in April that the measure it took against Iran's IRGC was due to its backing for Lebanon-based Hezbollah, which Buenos Aires blames for the deadliest bombing in the South American nation's history, a 1994 attack on the AMIA Jewish community centre in the Argentinian capital that killed 85 and injured hundreds.
